title: App Service plans, scaling and creating web apps
learningObjective: Pick an App Service plan tier. Scale up and out, by hand and with autoscale. Create web apps with the right runtime and settings.
foundation: Azure App Service hosts web apps and APIs without managing servers. The App Service plan is the set of VMs underneath, and its tier decides features and price.
Scaling up means a bigger tier (more power and features); scaling out means more instances of the plan.
Several apps can share one plan, and they then share its instances.
engineer: Tiers, smallest to biggest: Free, shared servers, no custom domains; Shared, shared servers, custom domains but no TLS certificates; Basic, your own servers, custom domains and TLS, up to 3 instances (scale by hand only); Standard, autoscale up to 10 instances, 5 deployment slots, backups; Premium v3, up to 30 instances, 20 slots, faster hardware, zone redundancy; Isolated v2 (App Service Environment), up to 100 instances, in your own network.
A plan is a set of servers: it's in one region and one OS (Windows or Linux). Every app on the plan runs on every instance. One busy app slows down the others, so give heavy apps their own plan.
Scale up vs scale out: scale up means a bigger tier. Scale out means more instances.

Ways to scale out: by hand (set the instance count); rule-based autoscale, Standard and above, using the same Azure Monitor autoscale as scale sets (VMSS), with metrics such as CPU, memory or HTTP queue length, and schedules; automatic scaling, Premium only, where Azure decides for you.
Creating an app: a name, which becomes <name>.azurewebsites.net and must be unique; code or container; runtime stack and version; OS; region; plan.

App settings: app settings and connection strings, which your code reads as environment variables; general settings (Always On, HTTP version, ARR affinity); deployment, from ZIP deploy, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps or a container image.
Moving an app to another plan: allowed, if the new plan is in the same resource group and region.

example.title: Putting small sites together
body: Five quiet marketing sites share one Standard S1 plan, which is cheaper than five plans. The busy checkout API gets its own Premium v3 plan, with autoscale from 3 to 20 instances and zone redundancy.

prerequisites: A resource group and a region
permissions: Website Contributor, Web Plan Contributor, or Contributor
limits: Instances: Basic 3, Standard 10, Premium v3 30, Isolated v2 100
portal: App Service plans > Create: OS, region, pricing tier.
Plan > Scale up (App Service plan) / Scale out (manual or custom autoscale).
App Services > Create > Web App: name, publish, runtime, OS, region, plan.
Web app > Configuration (Environment variables): app settings, connection strings, general settings.
configuration.cli:
az appservice plan create -g rg-web -n asp-web --sku S1 --is-linux
az webapp create -g rg-web -p asp-web -n app-contoso-shop --runtime "NODE:20-lts"
az webapp config appsettings set -g rg-web -n app-contoso-shop --settings API_URL=https://api.contoso.com
az appservice plan update -g rg-web -n asp-web --sku P1V3
az appservice plan update -g rg-web -n asp-web --number-of-workers 3
az monitor autoscale create -g rg-web --resource asp-web --resource-type Microsoft.Web/serverfarms --name as-asp --min-count 2 --max-count 10 --count 2
az monitor autoscale rule create -g rg-web --autoscale-name as-asp --condition "CpuPercentage > 70 avg 10m" --scale out 1
configuration.powershell:
New-AzAppServicePlan -ResourceGroupName rg-web -Name asp-web -Location westeurope -Tier Standard -NumberofWorkers 2 -WorkerSize Small -Linux
New-AzWebApp -ResourceGroupName rg-web -Name app-contoso-shop -AppServicePlan asp-web
Set-AzAppServicePlan -ResourceGroupName rg-web -Name asp-web -Tier PremiumV3 -NumberofWorkers 3

troubleshooting.cause: The plan is Free or Shared.
troubleshooting.fix: Scale up to Basic or higher.

troubleshooting.symptom: One app slows down every app on the plan.
troubleshooting.fix: Move the heavy app to its own plan.

comparisons.difference: Functions can run on App Service plans too, but they run code in response to events.
Managed app hosting. An App Service plan is a set of VMs you choose and pay for directly.

misconceptions.myth: Each app has its own instances.
misconceptions.reality: No. All apps on a plan share its instances.
No. Scaling up changes the tier. Scaling out adds instances.

architectureDecisions: Group apps into plans by load and lifecycle: quiet apps can share, busy apps get their own plan.
Production: Premium v3 with zone redundancy.
Apps that must stay warm: turn on Always On, so they don't go idle.

Pricing tiers and what they unlock

steps.label: Hosting
steps.title: A website without looking after servers
body: You want to deploy code, not patch operating systems. App Service runs the web server for you.

steps.label: Plan
steps.title: The plan is the server farm you pay for
body: An App Service plan sets the region, the tier and the instance size. Every app on the plan runs on the same instances and shares them. You pay for the plan, not per app.

callout.text: A busy app slows down every other app on the same plan.

steps.label: Tiers
steps.title: Tiers unlock features
body: Free and Shared: testing only. Basic: dedicated instances, custom domains and TLS, backups, manual scale. Standard: autoscale and deployment slots. Premium v3: faster hardware, more slots and instances. Isolated v2: a private App Service Environment.

callout.text: Slots and autoscale start at Standard. Custom domains with TLS start at Basic.

steps.label: Scale
steps.title: Up or out
body: Scale up = a bigger tier or size (more CPU, memory, features). Scale out = more instances running the same apps.
Autoscale (Standard and above) adds instances by rules on metrics such as CPU, or on a schedule. Premium plans also offer automatic scaling based on HTTP traffic.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: App Service plans
body: Pay for the plan; apps share it.
recap: Apps on a plan share its instances
Free/Shared → Basic → Standard → Premium v3 → Isolated v2
Scale up = bigger; scale out = more

handsOn.title: Create a web app on a Free plan and see the scale options
handsOn.cost: Free on the F1 tier. Do not leave a Standard plan running: it is billed by the hour.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.

steps.do: Search 'App Services' > + Create > Web App. Group rg-az104-lab, name app-lab-<yourinitials> (globally unique), publish: Code, runtime stack: .NET 8 or Node 20, OS: Linux, region: your region.
Pricing plan: create new plan plan-lab, choose Free F1. Review + create > Create.
Open the app > Overview > Default domain.
steps.see: The default 'Your web app is running' page.

steps.do: Open the plan (plan-lab) > Settings > Scale up (App Service plan).
steps.see: Tiers with their features. Compare Basic, Standard and Premium v3; do not change the tier.

steps.do: Open plan-lab > Scale out (App Service plan).
steps.see: On Free, scale out is not available. On Standard and higher you would see manual and rule-based autoscale.
The web app listed. More apps can share this plan.

check: You found the scale up and scale out pages and the tier features.
cleanup: When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
